events.text: A Ministry herald unrolls a summons with your name already copied into the margin. Two letters reach you on the same morning. One is from {hw_side}, one from {hw_foe}. Both say the war is just. Both offer a captain's rank. Both are sealed with the same brand of cheap wax, which tells you they bought it from the same merchant.

effects.log: You seal your reply with better wax than theirs. {hw_Side} writes back within the hour: you are expected at {hw_field}.
You burn both letters in the same brazier. The war goes on without you, for now, and both sides note it.

choices.text: Ask the wax merchant who else he sells to.

effects.log: The merchant names four houses and a pirate. You learn more about the war from him than from either letter.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries have posted the call to arms on every jade stair, in three hands of script. A recruiter from {hw_side} looks you over at the cloud ferry. 'No sect, no house, no backing,' he says, reading it off your sleeves. 'We take rogues. Front rank, half pay, and if you live you get a name.' Behind him a line of other unbacked immortals waits, pretending not to listen.

effects.log: He writes your name at the bottom of the roll. It is a start, and the bottom of a roll is still on it.
He laughs, then looks at you again and gives you three quarters. The line behind you stands a little straighter.
You walk off the ferry. Someone in the line says your name with respect, which costs you nothing and is worth something.

events.text: A marshal's clerk asks, very politely, which column of the ledger you would like to stand in. Your neighbour on the isle, a retired weather-weaver called Ok Danbi, has already packed for {hw_side}. She is old enough to have fought in three Isle Wars and loud enough to tell you about each one. 'Come with me,' she says. 'Or mind my goats. Choose.'

effects.log: You march with Ok Danbi. She talks the whole way and knows every shortcut through the cloud straits.
You keep her goats for the war. They eat your roof. When she comes back, she pays you in stories and a kid of your own.
She hits you with her pipe, gently, and goes anyway. You worry about her for a season.

events.text: A Ministry herald unrolls a summons with your name already copied into the margin. A broker of {hw_foe} comes to you before the other side can: he will pay spirit stones for you simply to stay home. 'Not to fight for us,' he says. 'Just not for them.' It is a lot of stones for doing nothing.

choices.text: Take the stones and stay home.

effects.log: You are richer and quieter. On the cloud road some people stop greeting you.
You refuse him loudly. The story gets to {hw_side} before you do, and they meet you at the gate.
He leaves puzzled. You did not want to be bought, and you did not want to fight. Both are allowed.

choices.text: Write back to ask her to stay out.

effects.log: She replies that she has never stayed out of anything. You knew that.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries have posted the call to arms on every jade stair, in three hands of script. A boy who runs errands on the cloud ferry, Mal-geum, has run away to enlist with {hw_side}. He is too young and too small. His mother asks you to fetch him back, or go with him and keep him alive.

effects.log: You find him in the recruits' line, holding a spear twice his height. He sulks all the way home. His mother cries.

choices.text: Enlist and keep an eye on him.

effects.log: You sign on beside him. The recruiter gives him a drum instead of a spear, at your suggestion.

events.text: A marshal's clerk asks, very politely, which column of the ledger you would like to stand in. Long ago you swore an oath to a teacher who belonged to {hw_side}. The teacher is gone. The oath is not. A messenger brings it back to you, copied out in your own young handwriting.

choices.text: Argue that the oath has ended.

ok.log: You find the clause that ends it. The messenger agrees, and seems relieved for you.

fail.log: The oath holds. You stay home anyway, and feel it like a stone in a shoe.

events.text: The Ministries' camp smells of ink, damp silk and the tea the clerks are never without. Two soldiers in the next tent have a bet on how many days the war will last. The stakes are their boots. One of them wants you to settle it by asking the officers.

effects.log: The officers do not know either, and are offended to be asked. Both soldiers keep their boots.
You guess the longest. Nobody wants to win that bet. The tent goes quiet.

effects.log: Ju Haneul goes. Nobody asks you. A season later a letter comes from the drifting isle.
The officer listens and gives him leave, signed. He is back in a month, a better soldier.
He stays. You do not sleep well after.

He gives up after a month, a little disappointed.

events.text: Your herald, Gu Ilhwa, is a weather-weaver with an orchard she misses and a voice that carries across three straits. She holds your declaration of war against {hw_foe} and asks to read it before she flies. 'Words like these last ten thousand years,' she says. 'I would like to be sure of them.' She has already marked two lines in pencil.

choices.text: Let her soften the two lines.

effects.log: Gu Ilhwa crosses out 'forever' and 'utterly' and flies off. The declaration that reaches {hw_foe} is hard, but it has a door in it.
Gu Ilhwa reads it out at the strait word for word. On the far isle, someone paints 'utterly' on a banner.

events.text: Your treasurer, Nam Sobong, a tidy immortal who balances accounts in his sleep, lays the war's ledger open. It is eating spirit stones faster than the veins can give them. 'Either the old houses pay,' he says, 'or the soldiers do, or the future does. Choose who.'

effects.log: The old houses pay and remember. Nam Sobong's ledger balances, for now.
The war goes on at full strength. Nam Sobong starts a second ledger, of what is owed, and it grows.
Nam Sobong balances the book. The soldiers fight a little slower.

events.text: Gu Ilhwa comes to you with her herald's staff in both hands. The war is older now than her orchard's youngest trees. 'I carried the first word of this,' she says. 'When the last word comes, let someone else carry it. I would like to go home while the plums are still on the branch.'

effects.log: She leaves the staff in your hands and goes. It is heavier than it looks. A basket of plums arrives at the end of the season.

choices.text: Ask her to stay one more season.

effects.log: She stays, without a word of complaint, and every morning she looks east toward her orchard.

events.text: Baek Yeonu, a young envoy of {hw_foe} whose family lost an isle in your war, comes to your camp under a white cloth. He has read the door in your declaration. 'You did not say forever,' he says. 'So I am here to ask you how long.'

effects.log: You talk until dawn. Nothing is signed, but both camps are quieter for a season, and he writes to you after.

choices.text: Offer him his family's isle back.

ok.log: He goes home with the offer. {hw_Foe} pulls back from the strait to think about it.

fail.log: He does not believe you, and goes home sure you are playing for time.

events.text: Baek Yeonu, a young officer of {hw_foe} whose family lost an isle in your war, rides out alone to the middle of {hw_field} and calls your name. Your declaration said 'utterly', and he has decided to take it personally.

ok.log: You beat him and let him go. He rides back very quiet, and you hear he has started reading poetry.

fail.log: He knocks you off your cloud and does not finish it. 'Now we are even,' he says, 'for one hour.'

effects.log: {hw_friend} fights him to a draw. Both come back limping and arguing about who won.

events.arc: The Defector of the Cloud Strait
events.text: At first light a captain of {hw_foe} climbs out of the cloud strait onto your isle, soaked and shaking. Her name is Mun Haeseol. She says she has had enough of {hw_cmdr}'s orders, and she has brought maps. Your quartermaster, Tak Bongsu, a gruff immortal who trusts nobody with dry boots, let alone wet ones, says to throw her back.

effects.log: You give Mun Haeseol a blanket and your own tent. Tak Bongsu counts the blankets pointedly.
The marshal takes her maps and locks her in a storeroom. Tak Bongsu nods his approval.

events.arc: The Defector of the Cloud Strait
events.text: Tak Bongsu brings you Mun Haeseol's maps. 'This ridge,' he says, tapping. 'There is no ridge there. Either the isle drifted, or she is lying.' Mun Haeseol, asked, says the isle drifted. She says it calmly, which is either very honest or very practised.

choices.text: Fly out and check the ridge.

ok.log: The isle has drifted. The maps are good. Tak Bongsu grunts something that might be an apology.

fail.log: You find nothing either way, and lose a day.

effects.log: You plan on her maps. The ridge is there, a mile east. It works, nearly.

events.arc: The Defector of the Cloud Strait
events.text: Mun Haeseol asks you for one thing. Her brother, Mun Ganghyeon, is still a soldier of {hw_foe} at {hw_field}, and since she crossed he is watched as a traitor's kin. 'Get him out,' she says, 'and I will tell you everything I know about {hw_cmdr}, even the parts I am ashamed of.'

ok.log: You bring Mun Ganghyeon across the strait in a fishing boat. The two of them do not speak for an hour, and then cannot stop.

fail.log: The boat is spotted. You get away. Mun Ganghyeon does not, though he is only put under guard.

effects.log: Mun Haeseol nods. She tells you everything anyway. That is worse to watch than anger.

events.arc: The Defector of the Cloud Strait
events.text: The war is behind you. A small cloud-boat lands at your isle with Mun Haeseol and a basket of salted fish. 'For Tak Bongsu,' she says. 'Tell him the ridge drifted.' She stays to tea and talks about the war as if it happened to someone else, which in a way it did.

effects.log: Tak Bongsu comes, takes the fish and sits down. By evening the two of them argue about maps like old friends.

choices.text: Ask what became of her brother.

effects.log: She smiles in a way that answers before she does.

events.arc: The Defector of the Cloud Strait
events.text: A letter reaches you from across the strait, from a soldier of {hw_foe} called Mun Ganghyeon. His sister was traded back in a prisoner exchange. She is under guard, he writes, and he is not allowed to see her. He asks if you know whether she crossed by choice.

effects.log: You write the truth. He does not write again. You hear later that he left the war, and took her with him.

choices.text: Tell him you do not know.

effects.log: You write that you do not know. It is kind, and it is not true.

events.text: You have brought the envoys of {hw_side} and {hw_foe} to a neutral isle. Eom Sajin, for {hw_side}, wants the peace to have his name on it. Hyeon Daeryeong, for {hw_foe}, is old and tired and wants only to retire to a fishing isle. Neither will speak first. The cook, Bae Ok, has made soup for twenty and only three people are eating.

ok.log: You bring Mun Ganghyeon across the strait in a fishing boat. The two of them do not speak for an hour, and then cannot stop.

fail.log: The boat is spotted. You get away. Mun Ganghyeon does not, though he is only put under guard.

effects.log: Mun Haeseol nods. She tells you everything anyway. That is worse to watch than anger.

events.arc: The Defector of the Cloud Strait
events.text: The war is behind you. A small cloud-boat lands at your isle with Mun Haeseol and a basket of salted fish. 'For Tak Bongsu,' she says. 'Tell him the ridge drifted.' She stays to tea and talks about the war as if it happened to someone else, which in a way it did.

effects.log: Tak Bongsu comes, takes the fish and sits down. By evening the two of them argue about maps like old friends.

choices.text: Ask what became of her brother.

effects.log: She smiles in a way that answers before she does.

events.arc: The Defector of the Cloud Strait
events.text: A letter reaches you from across the strait, from a soldier of {hw_foe} called Mun Ganghyeon. His sister was traded back in a prisoner exchange. She is under guard, he writes, and he is not allowed to see her. He asks if you know whether she crossed by choice.

effects.log: You write the truth. He does not write again. You hear later that he left the war, and took her with him.

choices.text: Tell him you do not know.

effects.log: You write that you do not know. It is kind, and it is not true.

events.text: You have brought the envoys of {hw_side} and {hw_foe} to a neutral isle. Eom Sajin, for {hw_side}, wants the peace to have his name on it. Hyeon Daeryeong, for {hw_foe}, is old and tired and wants only to retire to a fishing isle. Neither will speak first. The cook, Bae Ok, has made soup for twenty and only three people are eating.

effects.log: You seat them side by side over Bae Ok's soup. They do not talk, but they ask each other for the salt.
You open with what both sides already agree on. It is a short list. It is a start.

events.text: Eom Sajin takes you aside. He has written a draft treaty with his own name in large script at the top. 'It will help it pass at home,' he says. Hyeon Daeryeong, he adds, will never notice. Hyeon Daeryeong, at the far end of the garden, is noticing.

choices.text: Make him put both names, the same size.

effects.log: Eom Sajin sulks for a day and does it. Hyeon Daeryeong sends you a carved fish.
The draft goes forward with Eom Sajin's name on top. Hyeon Daeryeong reads it and says nothing at all.

events.text: Bae Ok the cook comes to you in the kitchen, very quiet. Her son is a soldier of {hw_foe}, held prisoner by {hw_side}. She has cooked for both envoys all season and told nobody. 'If it does not end,' she says, 'will you tell me where they keep him?'

choices.text: Find her son and bring him to the talks.

effects.log: Her son is brought to the kitchen under guard. Both envoys hear of it. The talks go faster after that.

choices.text: Make a prisoner swap the first clause.

ok.log: Both envoys agree. Bae Ok's son is first across.

fail.log: Eom Sajin refuses to put it first. It goes in as clause nine.

events.text: The treaty is ready, both names the same size at the top. Hyeon Daeryeong takes up the brush, then puts it down. 'I signed one of these once before,' he says. 'It lasted four hundred years. I would like this one to last longer. Your name is on it as witness. That means you have to keep it.'

effects.log: You sign. Hyeon Daeryeong goes home to his fishing isle. Every season he sends you a fish and a note: 'Still holding?'
You add a clause for the veterans of both sides. It takes another month. It is worth it.

events.text: The treaty is ready. Eom Sajin's name sits at the top in large script. Hyeon Daeryeong signs below it in a very small hand and says only, 'Good. Now I can go fishing.' The peace is real, if lopsided. In the corridor a young officer of {hw_foe} is staring at the large name.

effects.log: You tell the officer who really made the peace. It does not fix the name, but the officer stops staring.
You go home. The peace holds. It has a crack in it, and the crack has a name.

events.text: Cha Mudeok fought at the same strait you did, long ago. He is old now even by the count of immortals, and stubborn as a stone. The isle he held in that war sank into the cloud sea in the last battle, with his company's shrine on it. He wants to dive and find it. His granddaughter, Cha Seol, a sharp-tongued weaver, wants you to talk him out of it.

choices.text: Say you will go with him.

effects.log: Cha Mudeok claps you on the shoulder. Cha Seol gives you a look that could fold cloth.
You try. Cha Mudeok listens politely and starts packing anyway.

events.text: Ryu Pung, a cloud-diver with a cough and very good lungs, says he knows where the sunk isle lies: in a cold current under the old strait. He wants a fat fee. Cha Mudeok wants to start tomorrow. Cha Seol wants Ryu Pung's references.

effects.log: Ryu Pung takes the stones and buys a new rope. He is, it turns out, worth every stone.

ok.log: Ryu Pung takes half, laughing, because he likes Cha Mudeok.

fail.log: Ryu Pung walks out. He comes back next day, at full price.

events.text: You dive with Cha Mudeok and Ryu Pung into the cold cloud. The isle is there, upside down, its pines hanging like roots. The shrine is still bolted to its rock. On the wall are the names of Cha Mudeok's company, and yours is scratched beside them, small, as a guest.

effects.log: You bring it up together. Cha Mudeok does not speak for the rest of the day. He keeps one pine cone from the isle.
Cha Mudeok touches each name and lets the isle keep them. He takes only a pine cone.

events.text: Cha Mudeok is gone now, quietly, in his sleep. Cha Seol sends for you. On his isle a young pine grows upside down in its pot, roots up, needles down, from a cone he brought out of the cloud. 'He said you would know what to do with it,' she says, and she clearly does not think you do.

choices.text: Plant it on the old strait.

effects.log: You plant it on the rock above where the isle sank. Cloud-boats steer by it now.
She keeps it in her weaving room. Her cloth grows strange and beautiful patterns.

events.text: Cha Seol sends word: her grandfather went down alone with Ryu Pung while you were away. He came up after three days, cold and happy, with a single pine cone from the sunk isle. He wants to plant it, and he wants you there.

effects.log: You plant the cone in a pot on his isle. Cha Mudeok waters it every morning and talks to it.
He takes the scolding with great delight, like a prize, and then you plant it together.

events.text: Cha Mudeok is gone now, quietly, in his sleep. Cha Seol sends for you. On his isle a young pine grows upside down in its pot, roots up, needles down, from a cone he brought out of the cloud. 'He said you would know what to do with it,' she says, and she clearly does not think you do.

choices.text: Plant it on the old strait.

effects.log: You plant it on the rock above where the isle sank. Cloud-boats steer by it now.
She keeps it in her weaving room. Her cloth grows strange and beautiful patterns.

events.text: Yun Gwak came to the Upper Realm with no sect, no house and a sword she mended herself. Recruiters sneer at her sleeves. She wants a house to take her in, and she has decided the war is the way. 'Enlist with me,' she says, 'so at least one person in the line knows my name.' Her apprentice, a boy called Dong-i, carries her bag and has decided you are her friend.

effects.log: You put your names on the roll together. The recruiter, Seok Pan, writes yours neatly and hers as an afterthought.

choices.text: Wish her luck and stay home.

effects.log: She goes. Dong-i stays with you to wait for her, which nobody agreed to.

events.text: Seok Pan, the recruiter, has put the rogues in the front rank at {hw_field}, as he always does. Yun Gwak is at the very front, beside you. 'At least the view is good,' she says. Behind you, the sect-born soldiers are a long way back.

ok.log: The front holds. Yun Gwak's mended sword does the work of three. The soldiers start calling her Mended Sword.

fail.log: The front buckles. You both get out, barely. The soldiers who saw her cover you start calling her Mended Sword.

choices.text: Complain to the marshal about the order.

effects.log: The marshal moves the rogues back one rank. It is a small change. Yun Gwak, now called Mended Sword, never forgets it.

events.text: Word comes: an old house of the Upper Realm, the Hall of Pine Wind, has heard of Mended Sword and offers Yun Gwak a place. It is everything she wanted. There is one condition. Rogues they take in must give up their old ties, and that includes a certain apprentice who is not of good family.

effects.log: She refuses. The Hall of Pine Wind is so surprised that it offers again, without the condition.

choices.text: Tell her to take it, and keep Dong-i yourself.

effects.log: She takes it. Dong-i stays with you. She visits every season in fine robes, and they both cry at the gate.
She thinks a long time, then walks Dong-i to the Hall's gate herself and dares them to say no. They do not.

events.text: A letter from Yun Gwak at the front, in her bad hand. Seok Pan put the rogues in the front rank at {hw_field}. She is fine. She has a cut on her arm and a new name: the soldiers call her Mended Sword. Dong-i reads it to you three times, and then once more.

effects.log: You send the best you can afford. She writes back that it is on the wall, and she is still using the mended one.

choices.text: Teach Dong-i the sword while she is away.

effects.log: Dong-i is a terrible student and a tireless one.
